geos.label: South Bay
geos.blurb: San Jose, Saratoga, Sunnyvale, Mountain View

meta.standfirst: Arts, music, and worthwhile oddities, ordered by remove from Mountain View.

peak.note: 17 stacks up at Los Gatos from mid-afternoon
weekend beach traffic northbound in the evening
101 south through Sunnyvale is stop-and-go from 4
101 north is the worst of the peninsula — 280 is usually faster
101 north clogs from Redwood City at 3:30; the 280 split at Daly City is the second squeeze
weekend midday backs up into the city
the Caldecott is the pinch — eastbound clears by 7
Waldo Grade northbound is the bottleneck
Dumbarton eastbound is fine; the toll and the queue are on the way home
local arterials get slow around the school and commute peak

events.title: Comedy 101: O Brother, Where Art Thou?
events.note: The Coens' Depression-era Odyssey, shown as part of the Roxie's ongoing comedy-history series. The sepia grade still looks better projected than streamed.

events.title: Valerie June, Tianna Esperanza
events.note: Tennessee songwriter whose voice sits somewhere between Appalachian ballad and Memphis gospel — banjo, dulcimer and a register that goes thin and high on purpose. Two nights here; Monday is the easier ticket.

events.title: Cat Power: The Greatest Tour
events.note: Chan Marshall revisiting the Memphis-soul record she cut in 2006 — smoky, unhurried, sung barely above a whisper. A 500-seat room is an absurdly small place to see her, and the Peninsula almost never gets a booking of this size.

events.title: Azure McCall birthday concert
events.note: Bay Area standards singer with a long local history, doing the annual birthday set. Straight-ahead, warm, and the cheapest thing on Yoshi's calendar all week.

events.title: American Psycho
events.note: Mary Harron's satire, which has aged into something closer to documentary. Late show, 35mm-era crowd energy.

events.title: Death Guild
events.note: The oldest continuously running goth/industrial night in the world, six DJs across two rooms, 18+. Door time and price were not posted on the venue calendar — verify before going.

events.title: Bobby McFerrin
events.note: Ten Grammys, and still the only person who can hold a 600-seat room with nothing but a voice and a chest. One of three residency nights at the Freight this month. Set time and price were not on the listing that carried the date — check before you go.

events.title: Civic Center Soundtrack
events.note: Free lunchtime music and food trucks on the plaza. Booking is announced weekly and was not up at compile time; treat the act as unknown.

events.title: My Night at Maud's
events.note: Rohmer's third Moral Tale: two hours of Catholics arguing about Pascal and desire, and somehow the most romantic thing playing this week.

events.title: Sips & Sounds of Summer
events.note: Free Tuesday-evening set in the park near Left Bank, bring a chair. The venue's own page was down when this was compiled, so the act is unannounced here — the series books local covers and light jazz.

events.title: IV and the Strange Band, Clownvis Presley
events.note: Gothic outlaw country from Hank Williams III's son, with a Presley-impersonating clown opening. Exactly as advertised, which is the appeal.

events.title: Gipsy Kings featuring Nicolas Reyes
events.note: Rumba catalana from the Camargue — nylon-string strumming, group vocals, the songs everyone knows by the chorus. The hillside amphitheatre suits them better than any indoor room would.

events.title: Valerie June, Tianna Esperanza
events.note: Second of two nights. Same bill as Monday; if you can only do one, Monday's crowd is usually the quieter listen.

events.title: Nerd Nite SF #163
events.note: Three people give slide talks on whatever they are obsessed with, in a rock club, to a drinking audience. Running since 2003 and the purest expression of the oddities beat there is.

events.title: The Stylistics
events.note: Philadelphia soul in its sweetest register — Thom Bell arrangements, falsetto leads, 'You Make Me Feel Brand New'. Three nights, and the room is the right size for it.

events.title: Ida, Tara Jane O'Neil, Storey Littleton
events.note: Ida's close-harmony slowcore was the quiet end of 90s indie and has aged well. Tara Jane O'Neil opens with the same instinct for space. All ages, and a bill that rewards standing still.

events.title: Train to Busan — 10th anniversary
events.note: Yeon Sang-ho's zombie film works because it is really about class and a bad father. Ten years on, it still plays best with a full, loud room.

events.title: Los Mirlos
events.note: The Amazonian chicha band — surf-guitar tremolo laid over cumbia rhythm, invented in Peru in the early seventies and still played by people who were there. One of the week's genuinely rare bookings. Door time not published.

events.title: Exhibition tour: Maren Hassinger, Living Moving Growing
events.note: Free with admission, 45 minutes, on a sculptor who has spent fifty years making wire rope behave like foliage. The lunchtime slot is the least crowded way to see the show.

events.title: Hairspray
events.note: Matinee of the Playhouse's summer musical, running to 12 September. Their second stage, R.O.I., opened this month and plays the same weeks — the theatre listing this digest has otherwise been thin on.

events.title: Men At Work
events.note: Colin Hay fronting the Australian new-wave catalogue. A ticketing feed lists Toad the Wet Sprocket and Shonen Knife as support — an odd enough bill that it needs checking; the venue's own calendar would not load.

events.title: Angine de Poitrine, Population II
events.note: Montréal psych — Population II play a knotty, drum-led kind of prog that never settles. Sold out, so this is for people already holding tickets.

events.title: Deb Never
events.note: Grunge-inflected bedroom R&B, sung flat and low over guitars that are louder than the genre usually allows.

events.title: Drunken Noodles
events.note: Lucio Castro's follow-up to End of the Century — loose, erotic, structurally slippery. The Roxie is the only Bay Area house playing it.

events.title: Omar Courtz
events.note: Puerto Rican urbano act who went from SoundCloud to arenas in about three years. Listed for completeness — an arena is the wrong room for what he does.

events.title: Ne-Yo and Akon: Nights Like This
events.note: Two mid-2000s radio catalogues on one co-headline bill. Findable without help and priced accordingly, but it is the only thing at Shoreline midweek and the lawn is cheap.

events.title: The Stylistics
events.note: Night two of three.

events.title: Silkworm, Nina Nastasia
events.note: Silkworm played taut, funny, unsentimental rock for fifteen years and stopped in 2005 when Michael Dahlquist was killed; they play rarely and never casually. Nina Nastasia opens with the bleakest and best songwriting on any bill this week. 21+.

events.title: Pi'erre Bourne
events.note: Atlanta producer-rapper whose beats defined a chunk of late-2010s rap before he stepped to the mic himself. The Fillmore's chandeliers and free apples are the other half of the ticket. Door time not published.

events.title: Filoli Gardens Summer Nights
events.note: The formal gardens open into the evening, opening night of a run to 3 September. Which nights of the week it runs was not stated on the only fetchable listing — confirm before driving to Woodside.

events.title: Creative Resource Library: Synth Sessions
events.note: Open-bench evening in Gray Area's resource library — hands on the modular gear rather than a performance. Time not published.

events.title: The Sword, Red Fang, The Spoon Benders
events.note: Two of the better stoner-metal bands of the last twenty years on one bill — the Sword's Sabbath-shaped riffs against Red Fang's blunter, funnier take. Door time not published.

events.title: Free Wednesday at YBCA
events.venue: Yerba Buena Center for the Arts
events.note: Galleries free every Wednesday. Currently showing GaHee Park's Behind the Curtain — surrealist paintings that are prettier than they are comfortable. A panel, Creative Power Moves, runs the same day.

events.title: Downtown SF free outdoor EDM party
events.note: Ellis between Powell and Stockton closed and turned into an open-air stage. Free, five hours, and the DJ list was not published at compile time.

events.title: Third Thursdays on Treat: Treat's Got Talent
events.note: Neighbourhood talent show on a closed block in the Mission, with food, vendors and back-to-school tables. Small, genuinely local, and the first year they have run the talent format.

events.title: Summer Concert Series: Native Elements
events.note: Bay Area roots-reggae band on the grass behind the community center. Free, lawn chairs, and BART Colma is a ten-minute walk — one of the few Peninsula shows where transit genuinely beats driving.

events.title: Beats, Brews & Vines: Pride and Joy
events.note: Third-Thursday street party at Broadway and Hillcrest. Pride and Joy do Motown and Stax covers with a horn section — better than the format usually gets.

events.title: CatVideoFest 2026
events.note: Seventy minutes of curated cat footage, with proceeds going to local shelters. It is exactly what it says and the room is always full of people who came on purpose.

events.title: Luchino Visconti's White Nights (4K restoration)
events.note: Dostoevsky relocated to a fog-bound studio-built Livorno, with Mastroianni and Maria Schell. The restoration is the reason to go — it was shot to look artificial and now it finally does.

events.title: The Black Crowes, Whiskey Myers, Southall
events.note: The Robinson brothers are speaking again and the band sounds like 1992 on a good night. Long bill — doors are early and Southall goes on before most people have parked.

events.title: SF Bay Pop Fest night 1: Tony Molina, Galore, Paper Jam, Monster Treasure
events.note: Four nights of Bay Area jangle and power-pop. Tony Molina writes ninety-second songs with Thin Lizzy guitar leads and Guided by Voices brevity; Monster Treasure are the loudest thing on the pass.

events.title: Portraits of Past, The Saddest Landscape, Drought
events.note: East Bay screamo from the mid-90s, playing the record that half of the genre's second wave was built on. The Great American's balcony is a strange and excellent place to watch a band this loud.

events.title: G Flip, Vienna Vienna
events.note: Australian drummer-songwriter who plays kit standing up and sings over it — a genuinely physical pop show rather than a track-and-mic one.

events.title: BAILEN, BEL.
events.note: Three siblings doing tight, close-harmony indie folk — the blend is the instrument, and it only really works live.

events.title: The Stylistics
events.note: Final night of three.

events.title: Movies on the Square: F1
events.note: Free outdoor double feature — family film at 6, the main picture on the LED wall at 8:30. Caltrain Redwood City is three minutes away, which matters because the square's garage fills by 7.

events.title: Beach Goth Night
events.note: DJ night built on the surf-and-eyeliner end of the 2010s, cheap and late.

events.title: Scott Amendola with Fred Frith, Larry Ochs, Ben Goldberg
events.note: Four of the most serious improvisers in Northern California in a 150-capacity Albany bar — Frith alone has been redefining what a guitar is since Henry Cow. The best-value ticket of the week by a wide margin. Door time not listed.

events.title: Friday Nights at OMCA: Sabrina Shauna
events.note: Off the Grid trucks in the garden, live set, and the galleries open late — Mildred Howard's Poetics of Memory is the one to see. Outdoor block is free; the galleries are the usual admission. BART Lake Merritt is two minutes and downtown garages shut their gates at 7.

events.title: SF Queer Film Fest: opening night
events.note: Sixth year, three days, deliberately programmed around filmmakers Frameline's scale tends to miss. Opening night sets the tone and usually sells through first.

events.title: San Jose Cactus & Succulent Fair — evening sale
events.note: Forty-plus growers and potters, and one of the largest succulent sales in Northern California. Friday evening is the serious-collector session — the rare stuff goes in the first hour.

events.title: Music on the Square: Foreverland
events.note: Fourteen-piece Michael Jackson band — no wig, no glove, just the arrangements played properly with a full horn section. The best of the Peninsula's free Friday series, and the square fills early.

events.title: Wobbleland 2026: Excision, Alison Wonderland b2b NGHTMRE, DJ Diesel, Ray Volpe
events.note: Two days of bass music in a convention hall, 18+. Excision brings his own wall of subs and the room is not built for it, which is roughly the point. Adventure Club, Whethan, Lil Texas and Hedex fill out the bill.

events.title: Candlelight: The Best of Hans Zimmer
events.note: String quartet playing film scores by candlelight. A franchise format rather than a programme, but the Hammer is a real theatre and the arrangements are played straight.

events.title: Tucker Wetmore
events.note: Contemporary Nashville country with a pop-radio finish. Date sourced from a ticketing feed rather than the venue's own calendar, which was unreachable — check before driving up the hill.

events.title: Dimmu Borgir, Hulder
events.note: Norwegian symphonic black metal at full orchestral bombast. Hulder opens with something rawer and colder, and is the better band on the bill.

events.title: Mustache Harbor: Yacht Rock Forever
events.note: Soft-rock covers in a 1931 supper club with a mirrored backdrop, which is genuinely the right room for it. 21+.

events.title: SF Bay Pop Fest night 2: The Aislers Set, Kids On a Crime Spree, Lightheaded, Wifey
events.note: The Aislers Set made three of the best records ever released on Slumberland and then largely stopped; they surface every few years and this is one of those years. Kids On a Crime Spree share half a lineage and most of the same guitar sound. The night of the week.

events.title: Jailbreak at 50: The Rockers, Slough Feg, Buncrana
events.note: A Thin Lizzy anniversary night carried by Slough Feg, who have been playing twin-guitar heroic metal in this city for thirty years and do not need the excuse. Tribute framing, real band underneath.

events.title: Inner Wave, Pillowprince
events.note: LA five-piece playing loose, bass-forward bedroom psych with a lot of reverb and no hurry. Young crowd, and the Guild's sightlines are better than the price suggests.

events.title: DWLLRS, thebandfriday
events.note: Sun-bleached duo making the kind of loose, jazz-chorded pop that soundtracks other people's summers.

events.title: LCD Soundsystem vs Daft Punk Night
events.note: A DJ night pitting two catalogues against each other. No live band, and the listing says so plainly, which is more than most such nights manage.

events.title: MOUNT WESTMORE
events.note: Snoop Dogg, Ice Cube, E-40 and Too $hort — two-thirds of it Bay Area, and E-40 and Too $hort together is the part worth the ticket. An arena show, so no surprises, but the catalogue is deep.

events.title: San Jose Bike Party
events.note: Third-Friday mass ride, meet 7:30 and roll at 8. Route and start point are announced the week of; it is somewhere between a parade and a rolling block party, and entirely free.

events.title: Norman Brown
events.note: Smooth-jazz guitar of the Benson lineage, played cleanly and without irony. Two nights.

events.title: Gimme Gimme Disco
events.note: ABBA-led disco DJ night that tours the country. Standing weekly-format programming rather than a booking, but it fills the room.

events.title: Candlelight: Tribute to Coldplay & Imagine Dragons
events.note: Late seating of the same candlelit quartet format, stadium-rock catalogue instead of film scores.

events.title: Electric Duke (Bowie), Temptation (New Order)
events.note: Two tribute acts on a double bill. Real part of the circuit, listed accordingly — but there are four original bands playing within a mile of here tonight.

events.title: Niina Soleil, Rex & The Rhythm, Camille Trust
events.note: A three-deep bill of contemporary soul and funk revivalism. Late door at 9. Descriptor is lower-confidence — none of the three has much recorded output to check against.

events.title: Oakland Ballers vs Modesto Roadsters
events.note: First of three at home against Modesto. The schedule source gave an implausible first pitch for this date, so the time is unconfirmed — the Friday game is usually early evening.

events.title: Cocteaufest SF night 1
events.note: Twenty-third year of a Cocteau Twins fan gathering that has outlasted most actual bands. Night one on Folsom; the lineup and door time were not posted, but night two at the Chapel is the anchor.

events.title: Coyote Island, Mount Saint Elias
events.note: Sold out. Beer hall on Shattuck with a real stage at the back; the bill leans warm and folk-adjacent. Door time not published.

events.title: Block Rockin' Beats: 90s Rave
events.note: Big beat, acid house and trance played straight, 21+. Running alongside a 90s tribute-band night in the other room. No time or price posted.

events.title: Nine Vicious
events.note: A Fillmore booking with little recorded trail — the room is the draw more than the name. Descriptor is lower-confidence; door time not published.

events.title: Zola Jesus
events.note: Nika Roza Danilova sings gothic electronic music with an operatically trained voice, and the Freight's dead-quiet room is a strange, good place for it. Time and price not listed on the source that carried the date.

events.title: Pierce Warnecke and Matthew Biederman: Phytomorphic Topologies
events.note: Audiovisual work built on plant-derived forms, in a former cinema kitted out for exactly this. Closer to installation than gig. Time and price not published.

events.title: Oliver Koletzki, Course Correction
events.note: Melodic, faintly folk-inflected house from the Stil vor Talent label boss, with a separate bill running in the Loft. Flagged as a PW Picks night, which means the venue's membership programme gets in free.

events.title: Lupillo Rivera, El As De La Sierra, Rogelio Martínez, Leonel El Ranchero
events.note: Banda and norteño on a four-deep bill — Rivera has been a fixture of the regional Mexican circuit for twenty-five years and San Jose is one of his strongest markets. Door time not published.

events.title: San Jose Cactus & Succulent Fair
events.note: Full day, forty-plus vendors, free entry — competitive horticulture as spectator sport. The show tables are worth as much time as the sales floor.

events.title: Free Saturday: de Young Museum
events.note: General admission waived for the day, special exhibitions excepted. Pairs with the Legion of Honor, which is free the same day, if you want to spend a whole Saturday on it.

events.title: Free Saturday: Legion of Honor
events.note: The Rodin holdings and a colonnade over the Pacific, no admission. The 1 California and 38 Geary both get close; parking in Lincoln Park is easier than anywhere else in the city.

events.title: Oakland Chinatown StreetFest
events.note: Two days of lion dance, food stalls, local makers and a ping-pong tournament across closed streets. The largest free thing in the region this weekend and the one most worth crossing the bridge for. Take BART — 12th Street is a block away and Chinatown parking is hopeless during it.

events.title: Rockridge Rock-N-Stroll
events.note: Twenty-plus bands and fifty local makers spread along a mile of College Avenue — sidewalks and patios rather than a closed street, so the traffic stays and the scale stays human. Rockridge BART puts you in the middle of it.

events.title: Duboce ParkJam
events.note: Five local acts, an hour each, on the grass. Free, donation-supported, and the N Judah stops at the edge of the park. Bring a layer — Duboce catches the fog earlier than the Mission does.

events.title: The Sound 2026: music and arts festival
events.note: Free open-air Christian music and arts festival in the park. Lineup was not published at compile time.

events.title: Afrobeats at the Lake: Juls, DJ Neptune
events.note: Eighth year, two stages, forty vendors, seven hours by Lake Merritt. Juls produced for Burna Boy and Wizkid and is a better DJ than either's records suggest; DJ Neptune has been shaping Nigerian radio for twenty years. Kids under 16 free; parking is metered and hopeless, so BART or ride-share.

events.title: Bay Area Chocolate Chip Cookie Festival
events.note: A judged cookie competition on the lawn of a small technology museum. Free, three hours, and exactly as narrow as it sounds — which is the appeal.

events.title: SF Mime Troupe: WRECKAGE
events.note: Sixty-seventh season of free agitprop musicals in public parks, and still the only company doing it. Live music half an hour before the show; bring something to sit on.

events.title: World Arts West: legacy artist panel
events.note: Deborah Vaughan, Mythili Kumar, Naomi Diouf and Roy & PJ Hirabayashi in conversation — between them, most of the institutional memory of Bay Area world dance. Free, doors 1:30, reception after.

events.title: Pom Poko
events.note: Part of Some Nostalgic Place, BAMPFA's Isao Takahata retrospective — the one about shape-shifting raccoon dogs losing a war against suburban development, which is funnier and sadder than that sounds.

events.title: Wobbleland 2026, day 2
events.note: Second day of the two-day bass festival, same 6pm door and same 18+ rule. Single-day tickets exist, so this is the one to pick if you only want one of the two.

events.title: Non Stop Bhangra: Crash an Indian Wedding Party
events.note: Twenty years of dhol, Punjabi folk and club bass in the same room, with a dance lesson up front so nobody has an excuse. Early door for a Saturday — 6pm.

events.title: Montclair free outdoor cinema
events.note: Screen on the plaza in Montclair Village, free, bring a chair. Title was not announced at compile time.

events.title: Oakland Ballers vs Modesto Roadsters
events.note: Independent-league ball in a 4,000-seat park in West Oakland, and the cheapest night out in this digest. BART West Oakland is a fifteen-minute walk.

events.title: SF Bay Pop Fest night 3: Dear Nora, Jeanines, The Kitchenettes, Pillow Fight
events.note: Katy Davidson's Dear Nora writes short, plain, devastating songs and has been quietly influential for twenty-five years. Jeanines make two-minute jangle records that sound like they were cut in 1983 in a basement.

events.title: The Breeders, Imperial Teen
events.note: The Deal sisters in a 1922 movie palace, with Imperial Teen opening — as close to a perfect bill as this week produces. Both nights are sold out; the only route in now is a resale, so plan around it rather than for it.

events.title: Cocteaufest SF night 2: Simon Raymonde (DJ set), Sugar Hiccup, Mocteau Twins
events.note: First time in twenty-three years of Cocteaufest that an actual Cocteau Twin turns up — Simon Raymonde DJs from 8 and between the bands. The tribute acts are beside the point; Raymonde in a church-shaped room is not.

events.title: The Untouchables, The Inciters
events.note: LA mod-ska survivors from the early 80s, with Oakland's Inciters bringing a nine-piece soul revue underneath. A dancing show in a seated room, which usually resolves in the dancing's favour.

events.title: The Charities, Sweet Lew
events.note: Straight-ahead guitar band on a Live Nation-promoted bill; the room is better than the promotion suggests.

events.title: Norman Brown
events.note: Second of two nights.

events.title: Pearl & The Oysters, Chris Cohen (solo)
events.note: French-by-way-of-Florida duo making weightless, Stereolab-adjacent lounge pop. Chris Cohen opens solo, which is the quieter and stranger half of the evening.

events.title: Emo Nite
events.note: The touring emo DJ night. Standing format, listed for completeness.

events.title: Dust Breaks: Shakti EP release
events.note: South Asian bass producer running drum & bass, breakbeat and dubstep for a record release, 18+. No door time or price posted.

events.title: Little Stranger, Tropidelic, Jarv, Damn Skippy
events.note: Party-rap and funk four deep — a bill built for a room that dances rather than watches. Door time not published.

events.title: Jeff Parker and ETA IVtet
events.note: Tortoise's guitarist leading the quartet that spent years in a tiny Highland Park bar inventing a patient, loop-like species of jazz. On record it is one of the decade's best; live it is longer and stranger. Set time not listed.

events.title: SF Electronic Music Festival: 25th anniversary gala
events.note: Twenty-five years of the city's longest-running experimental electronic festival, marked in the room that has hosted much of it. Lineup, time and price were not on the calendar listing — worth chasing, because the anniversary bill is likely the strongest of its year.

events.title: Mismiths, Debased, Ceremony81
events.note: Misfits covers at the top of a three-band punk bill in a small Albany room. Door time not listed.

events.title: Generaiderz: LeNtO San Francisco — MURDER CLUB, exmantera, Gabberbitch69
events.note: Fast, abrasive club music across both rooms — gabber and hard drum rather than house. Door time and price not published.

events.title: Oakland Chinatown StreetFest — day 2
events.note: Same hours as Saturday and usually the calmer of the two days — better if you actually want to eat and talk to people rather than queue.

events.title: Festival of Chariots
events.venue: Robin Williams Meadow, Golden Gate Park
events.note: Ratha Yatra — hand-pulled chariots down the park, free vegetarian food all afternoon, kirtan and stalls at the meadow end. Six hours, entirely free, and one of the oldest recurring public festivals in the city.

events.title: San Jose Cactus & Succulent Fair — final day
events.note: Short final session. Vendors discount rather than repack, so Sunday is the bargain day and the picked-over one at once.

events.title: Lindy in the Park
events.note: Free swing dancing on the closed stretch of JFK, going since 1996. Beginner lesson at 12, no partner needed, and nobody minds if you just watch.

events.title: Montclair Picnic on the Plaza
events.note: Small hills-neighbourhood afternoon — food, a stage, tables on the plaza. Modest by design and pleasant for it.

events.title: Sunday Streets: Bayview
events.note: A mile of Third Street closed to cars and handed to the neighbourhood. The Bayview edition is the least touristed of the season and the most locally programmed. Muni T runs the length of it.

events.title: Golden Gate Park Band: a tribute to Ukraine
events.venue: Spreckels Temple of Music, Golden Gate Park
events.note: The city's municipal band has played free Sunday concerts at this bandshell since 1882 — this is its 144th season. Ninety minutes, no intermission, no ticket. Bring a layer; the Music Concourse fogs early.

events.title: My Neighbor Totoro
events.note: Miyazaki rather than Takahata, but programmed inside BAMPFA's Takahata series because Takahata produced it. A 2pm show, which is the right hour for it.

events.title: SF Mime Troupe: WRECKAGE
events.note: Second and final Berkeley date of the run.

events.title: Suds Francisco: funk and fermentation festival
events.note: Live funk and small-producer beer, cider and kombucha on the elevated park above the transit centre. Ticketed and not cheap, but the setting — a garden on a roof over a bus deck — is the reason to go.

events.title: SF Bay Pop Fest night 4: The Umbrellas, Artsick, WUT, Remedy & Wren
events.note: A matinee, which is the correct way to end a four-day pop festival. The Umbrellas are the current best argument that San Francisco jangle never actually stopped. Doors 2, music 3.

events.title: Oakland Ballers vs Modesto Roadsters
events.note: Sunday matinee to close the homestand. Afternoon ball at Raimondi is the best-value thing in the East Bay this week.

events.title: Grave of the Fireflies
events.note: Takahata's firebombing film, programmed immediately after Totoro exactly as the original double bill was — a scheduling decision that was cruel in 1988 and remains so. Sold out.

events.title: Keyon Harrold
events.note: The trumpet on Don Cheadle's Miles Ahead and a long list of hip-hop records, leading his own band in a room that suits him. The most serious jazz booking of the week, and the only one on this list where the horn is doing the writing.

events.title: Allen Stone, The Dip
events.note: Blue-eyed soul with real range, and The Dip are a genuinely good Seattle horn band rather than a warm-up. Date came off a ticketing feed — the venue calendar was unreachable, so confirm.

events.title: Built to Spill, PLAYDEAD
events.note: Doug Martsch playing long, unravelling guitar figures in a 500-cap room. Sold out, and it conflicts head-on with Keyon Harrold across the bay — if you have a ticket you are already committed.

events.title: Hippie Death Cult
events.note: Portland doom with an actual singer rather than a growler — heavy, slow, and more tuneful than the name promises.

events.title: SF Queer Film Fest: closing night
events.note: Closing programme, including the world premiere of In This Moment. Start time was not fixed on either the Roxie's or the festival's page at compile time.
